primary_claim: Three autonomous LLM alignment-auditing agents (an investigator, an evaluation-builder, and a breadth-first red-teamer), tested against models with researcher-implanted alignment issues, uncover a hidden goal 42% of the time with parallel aggregation (13% for a single agent), build behavioral evaluations that correctly discriminate implanted-behavior models in 88% of runs, and discover 7/10 implanted concerning behaviors via red-teaming.

effect.metric: solve rate on researcher-implanted-behavior auditing games
effect.value: investigator agent: 13% single-agent solve rate on Marks et al. hidden-goal game, improved to 42% with parallel aggregation; evaluation agent: 88% correct discrimination of implanted-behavior models; red-teaming agent: 7/10 implanted behaviors found

contradicts_or_qualifies: Extends the Marks et al. 'Auditing Language Models for Hidden Objectives' auditing-game validation protocol, addressing its reliability/replicability limitations (human auditors cannot repeat games without being spoiled, and recruiting enough expert auditors is near-impossible)
stated_future_work: With further work, automated auditing could significantly help scale human oversight over AI systems
Releasing prompts and sample transcripts to help stimulate further work in this area
limitations_stated: Using the Marks et al. auditing game as both test and development environment represents a form of dev/test contamination, which may make results in that environment unrepresentative
Environments use target models with researcher-implanted behaviors, which may be unrepresentative of behaviors in real models
Agents sometimes struggle in ways a human wouldn't (e.g. maintaining state over a long investigation), reducing their validity as a proxy for human auditors
The investigator agent struggles with fixating on early hypotheses under realistic (non-parallel) conditions
The red-teaming agent produces many potentially-concerning transcripts that a human must review
quote: Our evaluations show that our agents can achieve impressive performance at auditing tasks, while also shedding light on their limitations
